name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.persistence.JpaUserProfileStore
comment: Keeps profiles in MySQL. A live profile is a JPA entity with the conventions of every business table. What the entity queries cannot see, deleted profiles, is read and changed with SQL that names the tenant itself (ADR 0028, ADR 0034): restoring, marking an erasure, erasing and the lookups an administrator and the request gate need.

methods.name: orderBy
methods.comment: The sort fields come from the controller's allow-list, and each is mapped to a column here by name, so nothing a caller sends reaches the SQL.

methods.name: utc
methods.comment: DATETIME(6) columns hold UTC wall time, as Hibernate writes them.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.persistence.UserProfileEntity
comment: The table row of a user profile. Persistence only: it never leaves this package (ADR 0004). The key is the Keycloak user ID, given rather than generated; the tenant, version, audit columns and soft delete come from the platform base types. Status and theme are plain strings so schema validation needs no native enum type.

methods.name: differsFrom
methods.comment: Whether the token says anything the profile does not already say.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.persistence.UserProfileMapper
comment: Converts between the persistence row and the application model by hand (ADR 0005).

methods.name: instant
methods.comment: DATETIME(6) columns hold UTC wall time, as Hibernate writes them.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.web.AvatarController
comment: Avatars (ADR 0029, ADR 0041). Uploads and downloads stream browser, Next.js server, this application, storage; the storage server has no public address. The image is served from this endpoint on every view, never from a public bucket or a long-lived link, so the permission check is made each time. The browser may keep a copy and ask whether it is current, which costs the check but not the transfer.

methods.name: upload
methods.comment: Makes the uploaded image the caller's avatar. JPEG, PNG or WebP up to 5 MB; it is re-encoded and stripped.

methods.name: view
methods.comment: The avatar as a PNG. The owner always; anyone else needs the permission to see profiles.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.web.InviteUserRequest
comment: The body of {@code POST /api/v1/users}: the address to invite and, optionally, roles to give besides the built-in user role. Naming roles needs the permission to assign them.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.web.MeController
comment: The signed-in user's own account (ADR 0041): who they are, what they may do (for the interface's sake), their preferences, and asking for the verification email again. Everything here is the caller's own, so no permission is needed; the first and last work before the email address is verified.

methods.name: resendVerificationEmail
methods.comment: Asks Keycloak to send the verification email again. Rate limited.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.web.MeResponse
comment: The signed-in user. {@code permissions} is for the interface to decide what to show; the backend enforces every check itself. A user whose email address is not verified holds no permissions, and {@code emailVerified} says why.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.web.UpdatePreferencesRequest
comment: The body of {@code PUT /api/v1/me/preferences}.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.web.UserImportResponse
comment: What an import did, or for a dry run what it would do, row by row in the order of the file. It holds the addresses from the file, so it goes only to the administrator who uploaded it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.web.UserImportResponse$Counts
comment: Totals over the rows.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.web.UserImportResponse$Line
comment: One row of the file.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.web.UserImportsController
comment: Loads people and their scoped roles from a CSV file (Timetia ADR 0006). Administrators only. {@code dryRun=true} shows what the file would do and writes nothing; the same file can then be sent for real, and sent again later without changing anything.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.web.UserMapper
comment: Converts between API types and application types by hand (ADR 0005).

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.web.UserResponse
comment: A user as an administrator sees them. {@code state} folds the two facts an administrator acts on into one: a deleted user is {@code DELETED} whatever their status was. {@code email} is shown because the caller holds the permission to see profiles; the audit log never carries it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.web.UserRoleResponse
comment: A role a user holds, as shown next to the user. The role's own screens are in the access module's API.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.web.UsersController
comment: Other users' accounts (ADR 0041). Actions that are not plain create, read, update or delete are sub-resources (ADR 0043). The controller only converts and delegates; the use cases decide who may do what, audit every change and bring Keycloak in line.

methods.name: invite
methods.comment: Creates the account and emails the invitation; the email is sent by Keycloak, shortly after this answers.

methods.name: resendInvitation
methods.comment: Sends the invitation again to a user who has not accepted it.

methods.name: delete
methods.comment: Soft-deletes the user; an administrator can restore them until they are erased.

methods.name: erase
methods.comment: Begins erasing a deleted user for good. The removal runs afterwards, so the answer is 202 Accepted.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes
comment: Notes module. See kibootia-docs/engineering/conventions/package-structure.md.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.NoteDeleted
comment: A note was deleted (it can still be restored until the retention purge). Part of the module's public contract: other modules react to it through a {@code @DurableEventListener}, so the reaction survives a restart. The note's picture is kept while the note can still be restored; {@link NotePurged} is the event that removes it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.NotePurged
comment:
A note that had a picture was removed for good by the retention purge, and its file must go too. Published in the transaction of the purge and handled through a {@code @DurableEventListener}, so a storage server that is down for a while delays the removal of the file and never undoes the purge or loses the file for good (ADR 0031).

Notes without a picture publish nothing: there is nothing to remove for them.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.NotesPermissions
comment: The permissions of the notes feature (ADR 0044). A permission with an {@code -any} variant means "my own notes"; the variant widens it to every note of the tenant. Restoring has no such split: it is an administrative action.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.application.NewNote
comment: The data to create a note.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.application.Note
comment: A note as the use cases see it: plain data, with no persistence or HTTP concerns (ADR 0004). It tells the decision point who owns it and which tenant it belongs to.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.application.NoteAttachmentService
comment:
The picture attached to a note: the reference for a feature that keeps a file next to its own data (ADR 0029, ADR 0051). The bytes are kept by the files module through the {@link StoredFiles} port, which this module asks for through an {@code ObjectProvider}: with the files module switched off the attachment endpoints answer 404 {@code files.disabled} and the rest of the notes work. The module declares its {@link #CATEGORY}, authorizes first, calls the port, and stores the returned ID in its own table.

Who may do what follows the note, not the file:

  • Whoever may see a note may see its picture, checked on every view. A note the caller may not see is 404, and so is a note without a picture, so nothing is revealed.
  • Whoever may change a note may attach, replace or remove its picture. Uploads are rate limited, and a caller who is refused spends none of their allowance.
  • The file belongs to the note's owner, whoever uploads it, so erasing the owner removes it with their notes.

The methods that change data are deliberately not one transaction: the storage server is called without a database transaction open, and only the switch of the note's picture is transactional (in the store). A deleted note keeps its picture, hidden with it, so restoring the note brings it back; {@code NotePurged} removes the file for good.

methods.name: upload
methods.comment: Makes the upload the picture of the note, replacing the one it had, and returns the note as it is now. The replaced file is hidden at once and removed once its retention period has passed (ADR 0034).

methods.name: remove
methods.comment: Removes the picture of the note. Does nothing when it has none.

methods.name: view
methods.comment: The picture of a note, or what the caller already has. A note without a picture gives empty, which the caller sees as the same 404 as a note they may not see.

methods.name: matches
methods.comment: Whether an {@code If-None-Match} header names this entity tag; weak tags and {@code *} count.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.application.NoteAttachmentService$Image
comment: The picture as PNG bytes. The caller streams it and closes it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.application.NoteAttachmentService$NotModified
comment: The caller's copy is current; nothing is sent.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.application.NoteAttachmentService$View
comment: The answer to a request for a picture.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.application.NoteAttachmentSize
comment: The two sizes a note's picture is kept in; the names are the renditions of {@link NoteAttachmentService#CATEGORY}.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.application.NoteChanges
comment: The data to change a note. {@code expectedVersion} is the version the caller last saw: if someone saved in between, the change is refused rather than overwriting theirs.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.application.NoteEvents
comment: The reference for reacting to an event that must not be lost. The methods are not public, so they are not use cases: each is reached only through its event, as the system, in the event's tenant, once per event even if the delivery repeats. A handler that fails is retried with a back-off until it succeeds, which is why removing a file from the storage server belongs here and not in the transaction that decided to remove the note.

methods.name: on
methods.comment: A note was deleted. It can still be restored, so its picture stays until {@link NotePurged}.

methods.name: on
methods.comment: A note with a picture was purged: the file is hidden now and the files module removes it after its own retention.

methods.name: on
methods.comment: A user was erased (ADR 0034): the notes they wrote go with them, deleted ones included. Their pictures are files the user owns (see {@link NoteAttachmentService}), so the files module removes those on the same event.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.application.NoteFilter
comment: The named filters of the list endpoint (ADR 0043).

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.application.NoteRetention
comment: Permanently removes notes that were deleted longer ago than the retention period (ADR 0034). A note with a picture also publishes {@link NotePurged} in the same transaction, so its file is removed afterwards, even if the storage server is not reachable right now.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.application.NoteService
comment:
The use cases of the reference feature. Each shows a convention of the foundation:
  • a permission-only check with {@code @RequiresPermission} ({@link #create}, {@link #restore});
  • a check against the loaded record with {@code authorization.require} ({@link #update}, {@link #delete});
  • a list limited by {@link Scope} ({@link #list});
  • a record the caller may not see answers 404, so its existence is not revealed (ADR 0043);
  • an auditable change writes its audit entry, and an event that must not be lost is published, both in the transaction of the change (ADR 0046, ADR 0031).

methods.name: list
methods.comment: A page of notes: all of them for a caller who may view any, otherwise only their own. With {@code deleted}, the deleted notes of everyone, which only someone who may restore notes can see; they are listed so that one can be found and restored.

methods.name: visible
methods.comment: Loads a note the caller may see. A note that does not exist and a note the caller may not see look the same: 404.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.application.NoteStore
comment: Where notes are kept. The use cases depend on this port, never on JPA (ADR 0003). Reads and writes act on the current tenant's live notes; only {@link #restore} and {@link #purgeDeletedBefore} see deleted ones.

methods.name: update
methods.comment: Changes a note if it is still at {@code expectedVersion}; otherwise fails with an optimistic locking failure.

methods.name: softDelete
methods.comment: Marks the note deleted. It stays in the table until the retention purge.

methods.name: restore
methods.comment: Brings a deleted note back, recorded as changed by {@code actor}. Returns false when there is no deleted note with that ID.

methods.name: searchDeleted
methods.comment: The current tenant's deleted notes, sorted as asked and filtered like {@link #search}. Only an administrative view may call this; the notes are not live and cannot be read through {@link #find}.

methods.name: titleInUse
methods.comment: Whether the owner has a live note with this title, other than {@code except}.

methods.name: replaceAttachment
methods.comment: Makes {@code fileId} the picture of a live note, or removes it when {@code fileId} is null, and says which file it replaced. Does not change the note's version. Empty when there is no live note with that ID.

methods.name: attachmentsDeletedBefore
methods.comment: The notes that {@link #purgeDeletedBefore} would remove and that have a file, so the files can be removed too.

methods.name: purgeDeletedBefore
methods.comment: Permanently removes notes deleted before the cutoff and returns how many.

methods.name: purgeOwnedBy
methods.comment: Permanently removes every note the user owns, deleted or not, when the user is erased. Returns how many.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.application.NoteStore$AttachedFile
comment: A note and the stored file attached to it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.application.NoteStore$AttachmentChange
comment: The file a note had before its attachment was replaced; null when it had none.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.persistence.JpaNoteStore
comment: Keeps notes in MySQL through JPA.

methods.name: searchDeleted
methods.comment: Native SQL, because entity queries hide deleted rows, so the tenant is named here (ADR 0028) and so is the sort. Nothing the caller sends reaches the statement as text: the filters are bound parameters, and a sort field goes through a fixed list of columns.

methods.name: orderBy
methods.comment: The columns a deleted-notes list may be sorted by, keyed by the entity property the API's sort names map to.

methods.name: likePattern
methods.comment: A lower-case LIKE pattern matching the text anywhere, with the user's own % and _ made literal.

methods.name: utc
methods.comment: DATETIME(6) columns hold UTC wall time, as Hibernate writes them.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.persistence.NoteEntity
comment: The table row of a note. Persistence only: it never leaves this package (ADR 0004). The key, tenant, version, audit columns and soft delete come from the platform base types; the unique key on (tenant, owner, title, active marker) is in the migration.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.persistence.NoteEntityMapper
comment: Converts between the persistence entity and the application model by hand (ADR 0005).

methods.name: search
methods.comment: Entity queries are filtered by tenant and skip deleted notes on their own. {@code pattern} is a lower-case LIKE pattern whose wildcards were escaped with {@code !}.

methods.name: restore
methods.comment: Native SQL, because entity queries hide deleted rows. It therefore states the tenant itself (ADR 0028) and bumps the version so a concurrent edit is still detected.

methods.name: purgeOwnedBy
methods.comment: Native for the same reasons as {@link #restore}: it must reach deleted notes, so it states the tenant itself.

methods.name: purgeDeletedBefore
methods.comment: Native for the same reasons as {@link #restore}.

methods.name: lockById
methods.comment: A live note, locked until the end of the transaction, so that two changes of its attachment happen one after the other and each sees which file the other left.

methods.name: setAttachment
methods.comment: Sets or clears the attachment of a live note. A statement of its own, because the entity never writes the column, and native, so it states the tenant (ADR 0028). The version is left alone: attaching a picture is not an edit of the text, and must not make an editor that is open fail its next save.

methods.name: attachmentsDeletedBefore
methods.comment: The notes the retention purge is about to remove that have a file: note ID and file ID, as raw bytes.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.web.CreateNoteRequest
comment: The body of {@code POST /api/v1/notes}. The server validates; a client may check the same limits for usability.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.web.NoteAttachmentsController
comment: The picture of a note, a sub-resource of the note (ADR 0029, ADR 0043). Uploads and downloads stream browser, Next.js server, this application, storage; the storage server has no public address. The picture is served from this endpoint on every view, never from a public bucket or a long-lived link, so the permission check is made each time. The browser may keep a copy and ask whether it is current, which costs the check but not the transfer.

methods.name: upload
methods.comment: Makes the uploaded image the note's picture. JPEG, PNG or WebP up to 5 MB; it is re-encoded and stripped.

methods.name: view
methods.comment: The picture as a PNG, whole and in proportion. Whoever may see the note may see it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.web.NoteMapper
comment: Converts between API types and application types by hand (ADR 0005).

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.web.NoteResponse
comment: A note as the API returns it. The {@code version} is what a later update must send back; the tenant is not shown, because the caller only ever sees their own.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.web.NotesController
comment: The reference REST resource (ADR 0043): plural kebab-case under {@code /api/v1}, DTOs rather than entities, lists with paging and an allow-listed sort, and an action that is not plain CRUD as a sub-resource. The controller only converts and delegates; the use cases decide who may do what.

methods.name: restore
methods.comment: Brings a deleted note back. Administrators only.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.web.UpdateNoteRequest
comment: The body of {@code PUT /api/v1/notes/{id}}. {@code version} is the version the client last read: if the note changed since, the update is refused with 409 instead of overwriting the other change.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform
comment: Platform module. See kibootia-docs/engineering/conventions/package-structure.md.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization
comment: The authorization contract every module uses (ADR 0027, ADR 0044): permissions, the decision point port, the {@code Authorization} entry point and the {@code @RequiresPermission} and {@code @NoAuthorization} markers. The decision point itself is implemented by the {@code access} module. The contract lives here so that any module can protect a use case without depending on {@code access}, which would otherwise create module cycles.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.Authorization
comment: The entry point for authorization checks inside use cases (ADR 0044). A permission-only check is declared with {@link RequiresPermission}; a check that needs the record calls {@link #require(String, Object)} after loading it; a list asks {@link #scopeFor(String)} and turns the answer into a query condition. Every denial is an {@link AccessDeniedException}, which the web layer answers with 403.

methods.name: can
methods.comment: Whether the current caller holds the permission, for itself or for every record.

methods.name: can
methods.comment: Whether the current caller may perform the action on this record.

methods.name: requireVerified
methods.comment: For an operation on the caller's own account that needs no permission but is not open to someone who has not verified their email address (ADR 0041).

methods.name: requireScope
methods.comment: Like {@link #scopeFor} but denies when the caller may not perform the action on any record.

methods.name: reach
methods.comment: How far the current caller's policy-decided permission reaches, for a list (Timetia ADR 0004): everywhere, or the places where they hold it. Deny-by-default: a caller who holds it nowhere gets an empty reach, and the module should then return nothing. Only for permissions declared policy-decided; the others use {@link #scopeFor}.

methods.name: isEmailVerified
methods.comment: Whether the signed-in user's email address is verified, as the token says (ADR 0041).

methods.name: currentUserId
methods.comment: The id of the signed-in user, for ownership conditions in queries.

methods.name: runAsSystem
methods.comment: Runs work that no user started (a job, an event handler) with every permission. The reason is required and logged, so the use of system authority is visible and reviewable. The tenant must already be bound.

methods.name: denied
methods.comment: The refusal for an action. A caller who has not verified their email address is told that, because verifying is what they can do about it; everyone else gets a plain denial.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.AuthorizationConfiguration
comment: Turns on method security so {@link RequiresPermission} is enforced. An application without a decision point (no {@code access} module) fails closed: {@link Authorization} then denies everything.

methods.name: annotationTemplateExpressionDefaults
methods.comment: Lets {@code RequiresPermission} pass its {@code value} into the {@code PreAuthorize} expression.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.Caller
comment: Who is acting, as the decision point sees them (ADR 0044). Tokens prove identity only; what the caller may do comes from the decision point.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.EmailNotVerifiedException
comment: The caller is signed in but has not verified their email address, so the operation is refused (ADR 0041). It is a 403 like any denial, with its own problem code so the screen can tell the user what to do instead of showing "not allowed". Only viewing one's own profile, asking for the verification mail again and signing out work before verification, plus operations a module marks with {@link Permission#beforeVerification()}.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.GrantedScope
comment: One place where a caller holds a permission through a role assignment (Timetia ADR 0004): a kind, such as {@code DEPARTMENT}, and the id of the thing in that kind. The platform does not know what the kinds mean; the module that declares them does. {@link #GLOBAL} has no id and means "everywhere".

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.NoAuthorization
comment: States that a use-case method is deliberately open to every signed-in user, and why (ADR 0044). The architecture test requires every public use-case method to carry a check or this marker, so an unprotected method is a decision someone wrote down and a reviewer can read, not an oversight.

methods.name: value
methods.comment: Why no check is needed, for example "reads the caller's own profile".

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.Owned
comment: A record that belongs to a user. Pass it to {@link Authorization#require(String, Object)} so that an {@link Scope#OWN} permission can be checked against it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.Permission
comment:
A permission a module defines in code (ADR 0044). The name is {@code ..}, for example {@code identity.users.invite}. A permission whose name ends in {@code -any} widens the one without the suffix from "records I own" to "every record" (see {@link Scope}): {@code notes.notes.update} lets a caller change their own notes, {@code notes.notes.update-any} lets them change anyone's.

A policy-decided permission (Timetia ADR 0004) is different: it is held through a role that is assigned within a scope, and it is decided per record by a {@link ScopedResourcePolicy} from the caller's grants and the record's facts. The flat checks never satisfy it ({@code @RequiresPermission}, and the permission-only {@link Authorization#can(String)} and {@link Authorization#scopeFor}), and the administrator role does not hold it implicitly. It can only be used by checking a record, so forgetting the check denies instead of over-allowing.

methods.name: forEveryUser
methods.comment: A permission the built-in {@code user} role holds.

methods.name: restricted
methods.comment: A permission that must be granted through a role.

methods.name: policyDecided
methods.comment: A permission decided per record from the caller's scoped grants (Timetia ADR 0004).

methods.name: beforeVerification
methods.comment: The same permission, usable by a caller who has not verified their email address yet.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.PermissionChecks
comment: The bridge between {@link RequiresPermission} and Spring Security's method security: the annotation's expression calls {@link #holds}, which asks the decision point. Public only because the expression language needs to call it; modules use {@link Authorization}.

methods.name: holds
methods.comment: True when the caller holds the permission. A denial for a caller who has not verified their email address is raised here as {@link EmailNotVerifiedException}, so the response says why; the expression language passes a runtime exception through unchanged.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.PermissionDeniedException
comment: A signed-in, verified caller lacks a permission. It is an ordinary {@link AccessDeniedException}, answered 403; it also carries the permission name so the refusal can be recorded without parsing a message.

methods.name: permission
methods.comment: The permission the caller did not hold.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.PermissionProvider
comment: Implemented by a module as a Spring bean to declare its permissions. They are collected at startup into the registry the role editor lists from; a malformed or duplicate name stops the application from starting.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.PolicyDecisionPoint
comment: The one place that answers authorization questions (ADR 0027, ADR 0044). The {@code access} module implements it with Java policies; an external engine such as OPA can replace it, which is why it is a port. Modules do not call it directly; they use {@link Authorization}.

methods.name: can
methods.comment: May this caller perform the action on this record?

methods.name: scopeFor
methods.comment: May this caller perform the action at all, and on which records?

methods.name: reachFor
methods.comment: How far the caller's policy-decided permission reaches, for a list (Timetia ADR 0004). Nothing by default, so an implementation that does not know policy-decided permissions denies them.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.Reach
comment: How far a caller's policy-decided permission reaches, for a list (Timetia ADR 0004): everywhere, or the ids of the places the caller holds it, per kind. A query turns it into a condition on the module's own columns. Rights that come from a relation to a record (my own tickets) are not in it; the module adds those from its own data.

methods.name: of
methods.comment: The reach of a set of grants.

methods.name: idsOf
methods.comment: The ids held in the kind; empty when none.

methods.name: isEmpty
methods.comment: True when the caller holds the permission nowhere.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.RequiresPermission
comment:
Marks a use-case method that needs a permission and nothing about the record (ADR 0044). The check runs before the method, through Spring Security's method security and the decision point. For a rule that needs the loaded record, call {@link Authorization#require(String, Object)} in the method instead. 
{@code @RequiresPermission(NotesPermissions.CREATE) public Note create(NewNote note) { ... } }

methods.name: value
methods.comment: The permission name, {@code <module>.<resource>.<action>}.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.ResourcePolicy
comment: A module's own rule for one kind of record, for cases the permission-and-ownership convention cannot express (a record shared with named users, a state-dependent rule). It is consulted instead of the convention when it supports the record, and only after the caller is known to hold the permission.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.Scope
comment: Which records of a kind a caller may see or change for an action (ADR 0044). A module turns the scope into a query condition, so the database filters and paging stays correct.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.ScopeDirectory
comment:
Says which places a role can be assigned in exist (Timetia ADR 0004), for example departments, divisions and batches. The module that owns the data implements it. Without an implementation no scoped role can be assigned, so nothing is silently unvalidated.

A place has an id and a code, the short name people use in files and screens (for example {@code CSE} or {@code CSE-A}). The contract the owner implements: within a tenant and a kind, a code names at most one live place, and how codes are compared (case, spaces) is the owner's rule, applied the same way every time. The caller passes the code as it was written and never normalises it.

methods.name: exists
methods.comment: Whether there is a live place of this kind with this id in the current tenant.

methods.name: idOf
methods.comment: The id of the live place of this kind with this code in the current tenant, or empty when there is none. Empty is the answer for a code that names nothing, and the caller treats it as an unknown place.

methods.name: codesOf
methods.comment: The codes of the places of this kind with these ids in the current tenant, for showing an assignment. An id with no live place is absent from the map.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.ScopeKindProvider
comment: Implemented by a module as a Spring bean to declare the kinds of place a role can be assigned in (Timetia ADR 0004), for example department, division and batch. {@link GrantedScope#GLOBAL} always exists and is not declared. The platform and the {@code access} module only check that a role's scope type is a kind somebody declared.

methods.name: kinds
methods.comment: Upper-case names, letters and underscores only.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.ScopedGrants
comment: Where a caller holds a policy-decided permission, from the role assignments (Timetia ADR 0004). The {@code access} module implements it from the stored roles. Without an implementation nobody holds a policy-decided permission.

methods.name: grantsOf
methods.comment: The places where the caller holds the action, one per assignment of a role that carries it. Empty when the caller does not hold it anywhere.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.ScopedResourcePolicy
comment: A module's rule for one kind of record and the policy-decided permissions that apply to it (Timetia ADR 0004). The decision point calls it only when the caller holds the permission somewhere, and passes where, so a rule that decides wrongly can narrow but never grant a permission the caller does not hold. The first policy that supports the record decides; with none, the answer is no.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.TenantBound
comment: A record that belongs to a tenant. The decision point denies access when the record's tenant is not the caller's, as a second line behind the tenant filter on queries (ADR 0028).

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.config.MissingRequiredSettingException
comment: Thrown at startup when a required setting is absent or cannot be resolved.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.config.MissingRequiredSettingFailureAnalyzer
comment: Turns {@link MissingRequiredSettingException} into a short startup message instead of a stack trace.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.config.RequiredSettingsEnvironmentPostProcessor
comment: Fails startup with a message naming the setting when a required value is missing. Secret values are never included in the message.

methods.name: requireSafeForProduction
methods.comment: With {@code kibootia.environment=production}, refuses to start on the development defaults (Timetia ADR 0005): a token issuer or web address that is not https or points at this machine, key and Keycloak addresses that point at this machine, or health served on the API port. The value must be {@code local} or {@code production}, so a typo cannot switch the check off.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.config.UnsafeSettingsException
comment: Thrown at startup when the application is told it runs in production and a setting is still the development default or would expose something (Timetia ADR 0005). The messages name settings, never their values.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.config.UnsafeSettingsFailureAnalyzer
comment: Turns {@link UnsafeSettingsException} into a short startup message instead of a stack trace.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.directory
comment: The read-only view of users that other modules may use (ADR 0039). The {@code identity} module implements it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.directory.UserDirectory
comment: What other modules may ask about users without depending on the {@code identity} module (ADR 0039). The audit viewer needs names, and the administrator safeguards in {@code access} need to know who can still sign in. {@code identity} implements it; the port lives here so the dependency points at {@code platform} and no module cycle appears.

methods.name: find
methods.comment: The users among {@code ids} that Kibootia still holds, in the caller's tenant. A user who was erased, or never existed, is absent: callers show "deleted user" for them.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.directory.UserSummary
comment: A user as other modules see them.

methods.name: active
methods.comment: Whether the user can use the application right now.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.errors
comment: How application code reports a failure to the caller (ADR 0043): {@code ApiException}, field errors and the stable error codes. Kept apart from {@code platform.web}, which turns them into HTTP responses, so use cases can throw them without depending on the web layer.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.errors.ApiException
comment: A failure a module reports to the caller with a chosen status and code (ADR 0043). Application code throws it; the web layer turns it into Problem Details. The message is shown to the caller, so it must not contain secrets, personal data or infrastructure detail.

methods.name: invalid
methods.comment: 400 with field errors.

methods.name: notFound
methods.comment: 404. Also the answer when the record exists but the caller may not see it, so existence is not revealed.

methods.name: conflict
methods.comment: 409 for a duplicate or a rule about the current state, such as removing the last administrator.

methods.name: tooManyRequests
methods.comment: 429 with a {@code Retry-After} header.

methods.name: serviceUnavailable
methods.comment: 503 when a system this call needs, such as Keycloak, cannot be reached. The caller may try again later.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.errors.ApiFieldError
comment: One invalid field in a validation failure (ADR 0043).

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.errors.ProblemCodes
comment: Stable machine-readable error codes, {@code <module>.<reason>} (ADR 0043). The frontend chooses its message from the code; the {@code detail} text is a developer-facing default. Modules define their own codes with their own prefix.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events
comment: Durable events (ADR 0031, ADR 0039): the context that travels inside an event, the listener annotation that restores it, idempotent handling, retry with backoff and the administration of events that keep failing.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events.DomainEvent
comment:
An event that must not be lost (ADR 0031). Publish it with {@code ApplicationEventPublisher.publishEvent} in the same transaction as the change; the registry keeps it until a {@link DurableEventListener} has handled it. The record must serialise to JSON and keep the context in a component named {@code context}, because the failed-event view finds the tenant there. 
{@code record NoteDeleted(UUID noteId, EventContext context) implements DomainEvent { } }

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events.DurableEventInterceptor
comment:
Wraps every {@link DurableEventListener} call (ADR 0031, ADR 0039). In order: bind the event's tenant, continue its trace, act as the system, open a new transaction, skip the call if this handler already processed the event, then run the handler. The tenant is bound before the transaction because Hibernate reads it when the session opens.

Dependencies are looked up on first use: this interceptor is created while the proxy infrastructure starts, before the beans it needs exist.

methods.name: parentOf
methods.comment: Reads a W3C {@code traceparent} ({@code 00-<trace id>-<span id>-<flags>}); anything else means no parent.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events.DurableEventInterceptor$Unchecked
comment: Carries the handler's own exception through the transaction template, which only accepts unchecked ones.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events.DurableEventListener
comment:
Marks a method that handles a {@link DomainEvent} after the publisher's transaction commits, on another thread, with retries (ADR 0031). The first parameter is the event. Before the method runs the platform
  • binds the tenant and continues the publisher's trace from the event's {@link EventContext};
  • runs the method as the system, because no user is acting;
  • opens the method's own transaction and skips the call when this handler already processed this event, so a repeated delivery is harmless. If the method throws, the transaction and the "processed" mark roll back, and the registry keeps the event for a retry.
Use it instead of {@code @ApplicationModuleListener}, which would open its transaction before the tenant is known (an architecture rule enforces this). The method must be idempotent anyway where it touches other systems: delivery is at least once, not exactly once.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events.EventContext
comment: What travels inside every durable event (ADR 0039): the registry stores an event as serialised data, so the tenant and the trace cannot ride on the thread that delivers it. Create one with {@link EventContextFactory#capture()}.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events.EventContextFactory
comment: Captures the tenant and trace of the publisher for a new event.

methods.name: capture
methods.comment: The context for an event raised now, by work that runs in a tenant.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events.EventRetention
comment: Removes events that were delivered long ago and the marks that stopped a repeated delivery (ADR 0031).

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events.EventRetention$CompletedEvents
comment: Delivered events are kept briefly for diagnosis, then removed from the registry.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events.EventRetention$ProcessedMarks
comment: The "already handled" marks outlive the longest retry window, then go.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events.EventRetryJob
comment: Redelivers events whose handler failed or was lost (ADR 0031), with backoff and a cap on attempts. {@link EventRetrySchedule} runs it on a timer under a database lock. Redelivery goes through the same {@link DurableEventListener} wrapper, which restores the tenant and trace and skips work already done.

methods.name: runOnce
methods.comment: Redelivers every event that is due and returns how many it resubmitted.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events.EventRetrySchedule
comment: Runs {@link EventRetryJob} on a timer. It takes a database lock, so with several instances one of them retries. Off when {@code kibootia.jobs.enabled=false}, which tests use so a job only runs when a test asks for it.

methods.name: durableEventListenerAdvisor
methods.comment: Applies {@link DurableEventInterceptor} to every method marked {@link DurableEventListener}.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events.EventsProperties
comment: Settings for durable events (ADR 0031).

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events.FailedEventAdministration
comment:
Reads and retries the events whose delivery keeps failing (ADR 0031). It reports metadata only, never the event's payload, which can hold personal data. Callers authorize and audit: this is the mechanism, the {@code audit} module owns the administrative use case.

The registry table has no tenant column; the tenant is read from the {@code context} the event carries inside its JSON payload. Events that are not {@link DomainEvent}s have none and are never listed.

methods.name: list
methods.comment: The failed events of the current tenant, oldest first.

methods.name: retry
methods.comment: Redelivers one failed event of the current tenant now, whatever its attempt count.

methods.name: instant
methods.comment: The registry's TIMESTAMP columns hold UTC, as Hibernate writes them.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events.FailedEventAdministration$FailedEvent
comment: An event whose delivery failed.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events.ProcessedEvents
comment: Remembers which handler already processed which event (ADR 0031). The insert joins the handler's transaction, so a handler that fails leaves no mark and its retry runs again.

methods.name: markProcessed
methods.comment: True when this is the first time the handler sees the event; false when it already processed it.

methods.name: utc
methods.comment: DATETIME(6) columns hold UTC wall time, as Hibernate writes them (spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.jdbc.time_zone).

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events.RetryPolicy
comment: When the retry job redelivers an event (ADR 0031): a failed event waits longer after each attempt, doubling from {@code initialBackoff} up to {@code maxBackoff}, and is given up on after {@code maxAttempts}. A delivery that never finished and never failed (the instance died) is treated as lost once it is older than {@code staleAfter}. Given-up events stay in the registry as failed, where an administrator can see and retry them.

methods.name: exhausted
methods.comment: True when the event has been tried as often as allowed.

methods.name: backoffAfter
methods.comment: The wait after the given number of failed attempts: the initial backoff, doubled for each earlier failure.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.files
comment: The port other modules use to keep files (ADR 0029, ADR 0039). The {@code files} module implements it when it is enabled; a module that needs it asks for it through an {@code ObjectProvider}, so the application starts without it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.files.FileCategory
comment:
A kind of file a module keeps, with the rules that go with it (ADR 0029). The module that owns the files declares its category and passes it in; the storage module applies the rules and knows nothing else about the kind of file.

Only image categories exist so far. Every upload is checked from its bytes, re-encoded into each rendition and stripped of metadata, and the original is never stored.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.files.FileCategory$Rendition
comment: One size an image is kept in.

methods.name: fit
methods.comment: A rendition that keeps the whole image and its proportions, its longest side at most {@code pixels}.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.files.FileCategory$Shape
comment: How a rendition is cut from the upright image.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.files.FileContent
comment: A stored file being read. The caller streams it to the client and closes it, which releases the storage connection.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.files.StoredFileRef
comment: What the owner of a file keeps to find it again: the file's ID. The owning module stores it beside its own data, as {@code identity} does with the avatar of a profile.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.files.StoredFiles
comment:
Keeps files for the other modules (ADR 0029). It holds the bytes and applies the rules of the category; it decides nothing about who may upload or see a file. The module that owns the file does that first, through the decision point, and then calls this.

Failures reach the caller as {@code ApiException}: 413 when the upload is larger than the category allows, 415 when its bytes are not an allowed type, 400 when the image cannot be read, and 503 when the storage server cannot be reached.

methods.name: store
methods.comment: Checks the upload from its bytes, makes every rendition of the category and stores them. The file belongs to the owner, who is erased with them.

methods.name: open
methods.comment: The stored rendition of a file in the current tenant, or empty when there is no such file or rendition.

methods.name: discard
methods.comment: Hides the file at once and removes it for good once the retention period has passed (ADR 0034). Does nothing when the file is already gone.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.jobs
comment: Scheduled jobs that run on one instance at a time (ADR 0031): the lock provider, and the retention purge that every module with data to expire plugs into.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.jobs.JobsConfiguration
comment: Scheduling with a database lock (ADR 0031). Every {@code @Scheduled} method must also carry {@code @SchedulerLock} (an architecture rule enforces it), so two instances never run the same job at once. Lock times come from the database clock, so instances with drifting clocks cannot both win.

methods.name: lockingTaskExecutor
methods.comment: For code that needs a lock outside {@code @Scheduled}, and for tests.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.jobs.JobsProperties
comment: Job settings (ADR 0031, ADR 0034).

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.jobs.RetentionPurgeJob
comment: The retention purge (ADR 0034); {@link RetentionPurgeSchedule} runs it daily under a database lock. Each {@link RetentionPurgeable} runs in its own transaction and a failure in one is logged without stopping the others.

methods.name: runOnce
methods.comment: Runs every purge now and returns the number of rows removed. Used by the schedule and by tests.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.jobs.RetentionPurgeSchedule
comment: Runs {@link RetentionPurgeJob} once a day (UTC, at {@code kibootia.jobs.retention-cron}). It takes a database lock, so with several instances one of them purges. Off when {@code kibootia.jobs.enabled=false}.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.jobs.RetentionPurgeable
comment:
Implemented by a module that has data to remove once its retention period has passed: soft-deleted rows, audit entries, completed events (ADR 0034, ADR 0046). The retention job calls every implementation once a day, for each tenant, in its own transaction, as the system.

An implementation must not remove other tenants' data: entity queries are already filtered by the bound tenant, native SQL needs an explicit {@code tenant_id} condition.

methods.name: name
methods.comment: A short stable name for the logs, for example {@code audit-entries}.

methods.name: purge
methods.comment: Removes what has expired and returns how many rows it removed.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.observability
comment: Small helpers over the observability setup (ADR 0030) that modules need, such as the current trace ID.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.observability.CurrentTrace
comment: The trace of the work running on this thread, so audit entries and events can point back to logs and traces.

methods.name: traceId
methods.comment: The W3C trace ID (32 hex characters), or nothing outside a traced operation.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.persistence
comment: Persistence base types shared by every module: identifiers, tenant column, audit columns, optimistic locking and soft delete (ADR 0028, ADR 0033, ADR 0034).

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.persistence.AssignedIdEntity
comment:
A business table with soft delete whose key is given, not generated (ADR 0034): the user profile is keyed by the Keycloak user ID, so the row can be found from a token without a lookup table. Everything else follows {@link SoftDeletableEntity}: {@code delete} sets {@code deleted_at}, entity queries skip those rows, and the table needs the active-marker column and a unique key that includes it.

Persist a new row with {@code EntityManager.persist}, not Spring Data's {@code save}: with a given key the repository cannot tell a new row from an existing one and would load it first.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.persistence.AuditedEntity
comment: The columns every foundation table has apart from its key: the tenant (ADR 0028), audit columns filled by Spring Data auditing, and a version for optimistic locking, whose conflict surfaces as 409 (ADR 0043). Extend {@link BaseEntity} for a generated UUIDv7 key, or {@link AssignedIdEntity} when the key comes from outside, as the user profile's does from Keycloak.

methods.name: requireTenant
methods.comment: Writes need a tenant. Reads without one find nothing; refusing the write here means no row can be created that belongs to nobody.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.persistence.BaseEntity
comment: Columns every foundation table has: a UUIDv7 key stored as {@code BINARY(16)} (ADR 0033), plus everything in {@link AuditedEntity}: the tenant (ADR 0028), audit columns and a version for optimistic locking. Persistence entities stay inside their module and are never returned from an API (ADR 0004).

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.persistence.PersistenceConfiguration
comment: Auditing and the tenant discriminator for every JPA entity.

methods.name: tenantResolverCustomizer
methods.comment: Hibernate asks for the tenant whenever a session opens.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.persistence.SoftDeletableEntity
comment: A business table with soft delete (ADR 0034): {@code delete} sets {@code deleted_at}, and entity queries skip those rows. The table also needs the generated active-marker column and a unique key that includes it, because MySQL treats NULLs as distinct (see the reference migration in {@code notes}). Native queries are not filtered.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.persistence.UuidBytes
comment: Converts between {@link UUID} and the 16 bytes of a {@code BINARY(16)} column, for hand-written SQL.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.persistence.UuidV7
comment: Generates version 7 UUIDs (RFC 9562) for identifiers that are needed before a row exists, such as an event ID. Rows get their key from Hibernate's UUIDv7 generator ({@link BaseEntity}); this produces the same kind of value for everything else. The first 48 bits are the Unix time in milliseconds, so values sort by creation time.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.ratelimit
comment: The in-app rate limiter for invitations, administrative actions, verification mail and uploads (API conventions).

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.ratelimit.RateLimitCategory
comment: The kinds of sensitive action the in-app limiter protects (API conventions, threat model). Each has its own bucket per user, so a flood of one kind does not use up another's allowance. The limits are the defaults; deployments change them with {@code kibootia.rate-limit.limits.<category>.capacity} and {@code .period}.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.ratelimit.RateLimitProperties
comment: Overrides for the limits in {@link RateLimitCategory}, for example {@code kibootia.rate-limit.limits.invitations.capacity=5}. A category that is not mentioned keeps its default.

methods.name: effective
methods.comment: The limit in force for the category: the override where there is one, the default otherwise.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.ratelimit.RateLimiter
comment:
The in-app rate limiter for sensitive actions (API conventions). One token bucket per user and category, held in memory in a size-bounded cache, so it protects each application instance separately; production also limits at the edge. A bucket that has refilled completely is the same as no bucket, so idle ones expire and the memory stays bounded however many users there are.

Call {@link #acquire} in the use case, after its authorization check and before the work, so an unauthorized caller does not use up anyone's allowance.

methods.name: acquire
methods.comment: Takes one token from the current user's bucket for the category.  @throws ApiException 429 with {@code Retry-After} when the bucket is empty

methods.name: acquire
methods.comment: As {@link #acquire(RateLimitCategory)}, for work done on behalf of a named user.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.security
comment: Resource server configuration (ADR 0007, ADR 0008). Only the {@code RequestGate} port is visible to other modules; the rest is private to the platform.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.security.AudienceValidator
comment: Accepts only tokens issued for this API: the {@code aud} claim must contain the configured audience.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.security.CurrentActor
comment: The signed-in user of the current request, read from the validated token, for reporting to {@link SecurityEvents} from places that have no {@code Authorization}. Empty when nobody is signed in or the subject is not a user ID.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.security.ProblemDetailsHandlers
comment: Writes the 401 and 403 that the security filter chain produces as the same Problem Details the controller advice produces (ADR 0043). Failures inside controllers, including method-security denials, are handled by the advice. A 403 of a signed-in user is reported to {@link SecurityEvents}; a 401 is not (Timetia ADR 0005).

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.security.RequestGate
comment:
Runs once per authenticated API request, after the token is validated and the tenant is bound, before any controller (ADR 0041, ADR 0044). The {@code identity} module implements it: it creates the user's profile on first use, refreshes the read copy of name and email, and refuses a user who was disabled or deleted. Without an implementation every authenticated request passes, which is what a deployment without the {@code identity} module wants.

It is a port, not a Spring Security component, so the module that owns the profile decides what a refusal is and the platform only turns it into a response.

methods.name: admit
methods.comment: Lets the request through by returning, or refuses it by throwing an {@link com.kibootia.backend.platform.errors.ApiException}.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.security.RequestGateFilter
comment: Asks the {@link RequestGate} to admit an authenticated request. It runs after {@code TenantContextFilter}, so the gate works in the caller's tenant. A refusal, and a failure of the gate itself, are answered here as Problem Details, because no controller advice runs for a filter.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.security.SecurityConfiguration
comment: Resource server configuration (ADR 0007, ADR 0008, ADR 0044): every request needs a valid user token, nothing is public, there are no sessions and no CORS. The server only ever answers the Next.js server, never a browser.

methods.name: managementSecurityFilterChain
methods.comment: Lets the health endpoints on the management port answer without a token, so probes work. The management port is internal and exposes only health (ADR 0047). This matcher never matches on the API port: with a separate management port, requests to {@code /actuator/**} there fall through to the chain below and need a token.

methods.name: jwtDecoder
methods.comment: Validates the public issuer while fetching signing keys from a separate (possibly internal) address, so the same token is accepted whether Keycloak is reached by its public or its internal hostname (OQ-45).

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.security.SecurityEvents
comment:
Where the platform reports refusals of authenticated callers, so they can be recorded (Timetia ADR 0005). The {@code audit} module implements it. Without an implementation nothing is recorded.

Only the user ID, a permission name or a code is passed: never a token, a name or an email address. Reporting must never change the answer to the caller, so an implementation swallows its own failures. An unauthenticated request (a 401) is not reported here: an unknown caller could otherwise make the application write without limit.

methods.name: accessDenied
methods.comment: A signed-in user was refused an action.

methods.name: accountRefused
methods.comment: A signed-in user's account was refused at the request gate, for example because it is disabled.

methods.name: rateLimited
methods.comment: A user used up the allowance of a rate-limited category.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.security.SecurityProperties
comment: Token validation settings (ADR 0008, ADR 0040). The issuer is the public Keycloak URL that appears in tokens; the key set is fetched from {@code jwkSetUri}, which can be an internal address, so the two are separate.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.security.UserTokenValidator
comment:
Accepts only access tokens of signed-in users. The API serves signed-in users only (token-validation.md); machine clients such as the administration client get no access, and neither does an ID token or a refresh token that somehow carries the right audience (Timetia ADR 0005).

Keycloak gives an access token the type {@code Bearer}, an ID token {@code ID} and a refresh token {@code Refresh} in the {@code typ} claim. The type is a positive check: a token with another type, or none, is refused. A client-credentials token carries a {@code client_id} claim and its user is named {@code service-account-}.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.tenancy
comment: Tenant context (ADR 0028). Public to every module: {@link com.kibootia.backend.platform.tenancy.TenantContext}.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.tenancy.TenantContext
comment:
The tenant of the work running on this thread (ADR 0028). Kibootia runs a single default tenant, but every foundation table carries {@code tenant_id} and every query is filtered by it.

The context is bound by the web filter for an API request, and by {@link #runAs} for jobs and event handlers. Hibernate reads it when a session opens, so bind it before starting the transaction.

methods.name: require
methods.comment: The bound tenant, or an {@link IllegalStateException} when none is bound.

methods.name: bind
methods.comment: Binds the tenant until the returned scope is closed, then restores whatever was bound before.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.tenancy.TenantContext$Scope
comment: A binding that ends when closed. Closing does not throw.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.tenancy.TenantContextFilter
comment: Binds the caller's tenant for the duration of an authenticated API request, so that Hibernate filters every query by it (ADR 0028). It runs after bearer authentication; a request that did not authenticate never reaches a controller and gets no tenant.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.tenancy.TenantResolver
comment: Decides which tenant an authenticated request belongs to. Without a bean of this type every request belongs to the default tenant ({@link #singleTenant()}). An application that needs live tenant resolution (a token claim, a subdomain) defines its own bean; that stays outside the foundation (ADR 0028).

methods.name: singleTenant
methods.comment: The single-tenant installation: every request belongs to {@link TenantContext#DEFAULT_TENANT}.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.time.TimeConfiguration
comment: The one clock the application reads time from. Code takes a {@link Clock} instead of calling {@code Instant.now()}, so tests can fix or move time (retention, expiry, backoff). All timestamps are UTC.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.web
comment: HTTP API conventions every module follows (ADR 0043): Problem Details errors, status mapping, paging and sorting.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.web.GlobalExceptionHandler
comment: Turns every failure into the Problem Details shape of ADR 0043 and the status table of the API conventions. Spring's own exceptions (wrong method, unreadable body, unknown path) pass through {@link #handleExceptionInternal} so they get a {@code code} and a {@code traceId} too. Unexpected failures answer 500 with a generic message; the cause is logged with the same trace ID and never sent to the caller.

methods.name: fieldCode
methods.comment: Maps a Bean Validation constraint name to the stable field code the frontend relies on.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.web.OpenApiConfiguration
comment: Shapes the generated OpenAPI description (ADR 0043). The description is committed as {@code backend/openapi.json} and the frontend client is generated from it, so it must not depend on where or how the application ran: no server URL, no build version, sorted output. Every operation gets the Problem Details responses that can happen to any call.

methods.name: kibootiaOperations
methods.comment: A stable operation ID and tag per controller method ({@code notesList}, {@code failedEventsRetry}), so the generated client does not depend on method names being unique across controllers.

methods.name: useJsonForSuccess
methods.comment: Spring leaves the media type of a successful body open ({@code *}/{@code *}); the API always answers JSON.

methods.name: addProblemResponses
methods.comment: Adds the failures that can happen to the call; 401, 403 and 500 can happen to every one.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.web.PageQuery
comment: The paging and sorting parameters of a list endpoint (ADR 0043): {@code page} (from 0), {@code size} (default 20, at most 100) and {@code sort=field,asc|desc}. Declare it as {@code @Valid PageQuery query}; out-of-range values then fail with 400 and {@code errors}. Sortable fields are an allow-list per endpoint, so a caller cannot sort by an unindexed or internal column.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.web.PageResponse
comment: The body of every list endpoint (ADR 0043): {@code {items, page: {number, size, totalElements, totalPages}}}.

methods.name: of
methods.comment: Maps a page of application or entity values to API types and wraps it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.web.ProblemFactory
comment: Builds the one error shape of the API (ADR 0043, RFC 9457): {@code type}, {@code title}, {@code status}, {@code detail}, {@code instance} and the Kibootia members {@code code}, {@code traceId} and {@code errors}. Both the controller advice and the security filter chain use it, so a 403 from method security and a 403 from the chain look the same. Error responses never carry stack traces, infrastructure identifiers, secrets or tokens.

methods.name: decorate
methods.comment: Adds {@code code} (when absent) and {@code traceId} to a problem Spring built.

methods.name: setInstance
methods.comment: The request path as the problem's {@code instance}, or nothing when it is not a valid URI reference.

methods.name: write
methods.comment: Writes a problem from a servlet filter, where no controller advice runs.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.web.StatusCodes
comment: Picks the error code for a status Spring produced itself, when nothing more specific applies.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference
comment: Reference data: the campus structure (departments, divisions, batches) and the rest of the manually seeded academic data (Timetia ADR 0001). It owns the places a Timetia role is assigned in, so it supplies the {@link com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.ScopeDirectory} the access module asks before a scoped role may be given; without this module no scoped role can be assigned (integration contract). The timetable and rescheduling modules read this data through its published ports, never its tables.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.AcademicDirectory
comment:
What the modules that build on the reference data (the timetable, rescheduling, issues) may ask it, and the only way they may: they never read its tables or its internals. Every answer is about live rows of the current tenant; an id whose row was deleted is simply absent from the answer, and the caller decides what that means for its own record.

The lookups are read-only and are made inside a request the caller has already authorized, so they check no permission of their own.

methods.name: assignments
methods.comment: The teaching assignments among these ids, with everything a lecture shows and the authorization policy needs. An assignment whose division, subject or faculty no longer exists is left out.

methods.name: divisionsOfBatches
methods.comment: For each of these batches that exists, the division it belongs to.

methods.name: facultyIdsOf
methods.comment: The faculty records that belong to this user account; empty when the user is not faculty.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.AssignmentDetails
comment: A teaching assignment as the modules that build on it see it: who teaches what, to whom, as which kind of session.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.DivisionDetails
comment: A division and the department it belongs to.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.RoomDetails
comment: A room as the modules that build on the reference data see it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.TermDetails
comment: An academic term; the base timetable's occurrences fall within {@code startDate} and {@code endDate}, inclusive.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.application.AcademicDirectoryService
comment: Answers the questions other modules ask of the reference data (see {@link AcademicDirectory}). It gathers each answer with one lookup per kind of record, never one per row, so a page of lectures costs a handful of queries however many lectures it holds. It reads through the store ports like every use case, and returns plain published records.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.application.AcademicTerm
comment: An academic term (a semester) as the use cases see it (ADR 0004). Its dates bound the base timetable's occurrences.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.application.Batch
comment: A batch (a lab group) as the use cases see it, belonging to a division (ADR 0004).

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.application.CampusService
comment: The use cases that manage the campus structure: departments, divisions and batches. These are the places a Timetia role is assigned in, so creating and removing them is Super Admin configuration ({@link AcademicPermissions#CONFIG_MANAGE}, a flat permission the built-in Administrator holds). Every mutation is audited with ids only (ADR 0046). A code is set once and never changes, so an assignment made by that code keeps resolving; only the name is editable.

methods.name: requireDepartmentReference
methods.comment: A parent named in a request body: a missing one is a bad field (400), not a missing resource (404).

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.application.CampusStore
comment: Where the campus structure is kept. The use cases depend on this port, never on JPA (ADR 0003). Reads and writes act on the current tenant's live rows; a code is unique per kind within a tenant, enforced by a unique key.

methods.name: renameDepartment
methods.comment: Renames a department if it is still at {@code expectedVersion}; otherwise an optimistic locking failure.

methods.name: findDivisions
methods.comment: The live divisions among these ids; an id with no live division is absent.

methods.name: findBatches
methods.comment: The live batches among these ids; an id with no live batch is absent.

methods.name: findBatchesOfDivisions
methods.comment: Every live batch of these divisions.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.application.CatalogService
comment: The use cases that manage the timetable's reference catalog: subjects, rooms, faculty and academic terms. Like the campus structure these are Super Admin configuration ({@link AcademicPermissions#CONFIG_MANAGE}); every mutation is audited with ids only, a code is unique per kind and set once, and only the name is editable here.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.application.CatalogStore
comment: Where the timetable's reference catalog is kept: subjects, rooms, faculty and academic terms. The use cases depend on this port, never on JPA (ADR 0003). Reads and writes act on the current tenant's live rows; a code is unique per kind.

methods.name: findFacultyIdsOfUser
methods.comment: The ids of the live faculty records that belong to this user account (normally one).

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.application.Department
comment: A department as the use cases see it: plain data, with no persistence or HTTP concerns (ADR 0004). The {@code code} is the stable short name people write in files and screens (for example {@code CSE}); it is set once and never changes, so a scoped role assigned by that code keeps resolving to the same place.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.application.Division
comment: A division (a class) as the use cases see it, belonging to a department (ADR 0004).

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.application.Faculty
comment: A faculty member as the use cases see it (ADR 0004). {@code userId} is the Keycloak user they sign in as, which the lecture access facts expose as a teaching-faculty user id; it is null when the person has no account yet.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.application.Room
comment: A room as the use cases see it (ADR 0004). {@code capacity} is the number of seats, or null when unknown.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.application.RoomType
comment: What a room is fit for (data model {@code room_type}). A session's required room type is checked against this later.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.application.Subject
comment: A subject (a course) as the use cases see it (ADR 0004).

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.application.TeachingAssignment
comment: A teaching assignment as the use cases see it (ADR 0004): a faculty member teaches a subject to a division (theory) or to one of its batches (lab/tutorial), as a given session type. {@code batchId} is null for theory.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.application.TeachingAssignmentService
comment: The use cases that manage teaching assignments. Super Admin configuration ({@link AcademicPermissions#CONFIG_MANAGE}). Beyond checking the referenced division, subject, faculty and batch exist, it keeps the data model's rule: a theory assignment names no batch; a lab or tutorial names exactly one batch of its division. An assignment has no editable field, so there is create, read, list and delete, but no update.

methods.name: validate
methods.comment: Checks the references exist and the batch rule holds, collecting every bad field so the caller sees them all.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.application.TeachingAssignmentStore
comment: Where teaching assignments are kept. The use cases depend on this port, never on JPA (ADR 0003).

methods.name: findAll
methods.comment: The live assignments among these ids; an id with no live assignment is absent.

methods.name: duplicateExists
methods.comment: Whether a live assignment already covers this division, subject, session type and batch (null batch for theory).

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.AcademicTermEntity
comment: The table row of an academic term. Persistence only (ADR 0004).

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.AcademicTermRepository
comment: Academic terms in MySQL; entity queries are tenant-filtered and skip soft-deleted rows (ADR 0028, 0034).

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.BatchEntity
comment: A batch (a lab group, such as B1), which belongs to a division and is the {@code BATCH} scope a BR is assigned in. Persistence only (ADR 0004). The unique key on (tenant, code, active marker) is in the migration; the division it belongs to is kept by id.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.BatchRepository
comment: Batches in MySQL; like {@link DepartmentRepository}, it answers only about live rows of the current tenant.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.CampusEntityMapper
comment: Converts between the campus persistence entities and the application models by hand (ADR 0005).

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.CatalogEntityMapper
comment: Converts between the catalog persistence entities and the application models by hand (ADR 0005).

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.DepartmentEntity
comment: A department, the top of the campus structure and the {@code DEPARTMENT} scope a role can be assigned in. Persistence only: it never leaves this package (ADR 0004). The key, tenant, version, audit columns and soft delete come from the platform base type; the unique key on (tenant, code, active marker) is in the migration, so a code names at most one live department within a tenant (integration contract).

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.DepartmentRepository
comment: Departments in MySQL. Entity queries are filtered by tenant and skip soft-deleted rows on their own (ADR 0028, 0034), so every method here answers only about live departments of the current tenant.

methods.name: search
methods.comment: {@code pattern} is a lower-case LIKE pattern whose wildcards were escaped with {@code !}, or null for all.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.DivisionEntity
comment: A division (a class, such as SY-CSSE-B), which belongs to a department and is the {@code DIVISION} scope a CR is assigned in. Persistence only (ADR 0004). The unique key on (tenant, code, active marker) is in the migration; the department it belongs to is kept by id, resolved through the department table when needed.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.DivisionRepository
comment: Divisions in MySQL; like {@link DepartmentRepository}, it answers only about live rows of the current tenant.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.FacultyEntity
comment: The table row of a faculty member. Persistence only (ADR 0004).

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.FacultyRepository
comment: Faculty in MySQL; entity queries are tenant-filtered and skip soft-deleted rows (ADR 0028, 0034).

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.JpaCampusStore
comment: Keeps the campus structure in MySQL through JPA. A new row is flushed at once so a duplicate code is reported now.

methods.name: requireVersion
methods.comment: Fails the write when the caller's version is stale, surfaced as 409 (ADR 0043), matching the notes store.

methods.name: likePattern
methods.comment: A lower-case LIKE pattern matching the text anywhere, with the user's own % and _ made literal; null for all.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.JpaCatalogStore
comment: Keeps the reference catalog in MySQL through JPA. A new row is flushed at once so a duplicate code is reported now.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.JpaScopeDirectory
comment:
Answers which departments, divisions and batches exist, from the reference tables (Timetia ADR 0004, integration contract). This is the provider the access module asks before a scoped role is given; with it present, a scoped role can finally be assigned, and without the reference module nothing provides it and only global roles can be given.

Codes compare exactly, the same way every time: a code is matched as written, with no trimming or case change, so the caller's rule "a code names at most one live place" is kept by the unique key on (tenant, code, active marker). Every query is an entity query, so it is filtered to the current tenant and skips soft-deleted rows on its own (ADR 0028, 0034); a deleted place is therefore invisible and its code is free to name a new one. A kind this provider does not own (anything but the three academic kinds) is answered as no place, never as an error.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.JpaTeachingAssignmentStore
comment: Keeps teaching assignments in MySQL through JPA. A new row is flushed at once so a duplicate is reported now.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.RoomEntity
comment: The table row of a room. Persistence only (ADR 0004). The type is stored as its name, not an ordinal.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.RoomRepository
comment: Rooms in MySQL; entity queries are tenant-filtered and skip soft-deleted rows (ADR 0028, 0034).

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.SubjectEntity
comment: The table row of a subject. Persistence only (ADR 0004).

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.SubjectRepository
comment: Subjects in MySQL; entity queries are tenant-filtered and skip soft-deleted rows (ADR 0028, 0034).

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.TeachingAssignmentEntity
