name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable
comment: Timetable module: a division's manually arranged base timetable (Timetia ADR 0001), published as dated lectures, and the live view of them. It owns versions, weekly entries and the lectures on each date; it reads the reference data only through {@link com.kibootia.backend.reference.AcademicDirectory}, and builds the facts the authorization policy needs ({@link com.kibootia.backend.academic.LectureAccessFacts}) for the lectures it owns. Changes to a lecture are the rescheduling module's business and are laid over this base, never written into it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.ChangeConflictException
comment: A change was refused because of conflicts. Nothing was written when it is thrown, which is why the port's {@code apply} does not mark the caller's transaction for rollback: the caller can record the conflicts and commit.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.ConflictType
comment: Why a change cannot be made (data model {@code conflict_type}). Every one blocks; nobody can override a conflict (conflict rules). Room fit (type and seats) is not checked yet, because the data it needs, what each kind of session requires and the strength of a division, is not held.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.LectureCalendar
comment:
The live timetable as the rescheduling module uses it: read a lecture as it is now, ask whether changes can be made, and make them. The timetable owns the lectures and the resources they hold, so the rules that keep a teacher, a room or a group of students from being booked twice live here, and a change is made all or nothing.

The module that calls this decides who may change a lecture and whether a ticket is in a state to be applied; the calls check no permission of their own. They are not for a request that has not been authorized.

methods.name: lecture
methods.comment: The lecture as it is now, or empty when there is no such live lecture.

methods.name: zone
methods.comment: The time zone of the campus, in which hours are read and a lecture is said to have started.

methods.name: check
methods.comment: What would stop these changes, without making them. Changes made together are checked together: a lecture moving out of a slot frees it for another that moves in. Empty means they can be made.

methods.name: apply
methods.comment: Makes the changes, all or none, and records the ticket that made them. The lectures are locked and the changes checked again first.  @throws ChangeConflictException when something stops them; nothing was written

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.LectureChange
comment: A change to one lecture: move it to {@code target}, or cancel it when {@code target} is null. It is made against the state the lecture was in when the change was planned: if the lecture has changed since ({@code expectedRevision} no longer matches), the change is refused, so a ticket never overwrites what another ticket did.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.LectureConflict
comment: One reason a change cannot be made.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.LectureMode
comment: How a lecture is held (data model {@code lecture_mode}). An in-person lecture has a room and an online one has none, but may carry a meeting link.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.LectureSlot
comment: Where and when one lecture is held: the date, the hours, and how. It describes a lecture as the base timetable has it, as it is now after changes, and as a change would leave it.

methods.name: hours
methods.comment: How many whole hours the lecture lasts; a lecture starts and ends on the hour.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.LectureView
comment:
One lecture on one date as it is now: the base timetable's slot with any applied change laid over it, who it is for and who teaches it, with everything the authorization policy needs. It is what the live timetable shows and what the rescheduling module reads, so the two never disagree about a lecture.

The batches the lecture is for and the account the faculty member signs in as are those of the reference data now, so a new batch or a newly linked account applies at once. A name or code is null when what it describes was deleted since the timetable was published.

methods.name: changed
methods.comment: Whether a change has been laid over this lecture.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.TimetableConfiguration
comment: Switches on the timetable module's settings.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.application.ClaimStore
comment: Where what each lecture holds is kept (see {@link com.kibootia.backend.timetable.domain.Claims}). The use cases depend on this port, never on JPA (ADR 0003). Two claims never have the same key: the store refuses the second, which is the last defence against two changes racing for one slot.

methods.name: insertAll
methods.comment: Stores the claims. Fails with a data integrity violation when one of the keys is already held.

methods.name: deleteOf
methods.comment: Releases everything these lectures hold.

methods.name: holders
methods.comment: For each of these keys that is held, the lecture that holds it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.application.ClaimStore$Claim
comment: What one lecture holds.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.application.LectureCalendarService
comment:
Reads lectures as they are now and makes changes to them, for the rescheduling module. The rule it keeps: a teacher, a room or a group of students is never in two lectures at once. Every lecture holds claims on those things for each hour (see {@link Claims}); a change is allowed only when nothing it needs is held by another lecture, and the claims move with the lecture in the same transaction, so what is held always matches what is scheduled.

Checking tells the person planning a change what is in the way. Applying checks again with the lectures locked, because something may have changed since, and the unique key on the claims decides if two changes still race for one slot. Lectures changed together are checked together: a lecture moving out of a slot frees it for one moving in.

methods.name: apply
methods.comment: Not marked for rollback when it refuses the changes: it has written nothing by then, and the caller records the conflicts and commits.

methods.name: claimsOf
methods.comment: What the lecture needs once it is at {@code slot}.

methods.name: typeOf
methods.comment: A lecture another ticket moved into the slot is a clash of tickets; otherwise what is held says what is in the way.

methods.name: calendarProblems
methods.comment: The calendar: never a Sunday, never outside the term, and always on the hour between 08:00 and 20:00.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.application.LectureViewFactory
comment: Turns stored lectures into the {@link LectureView} that the live timetable and the rescheduling module both read. What a lecture is for and who teaches it are looked up in the reference data as it is now, once for a whole page and not once per lecture, so a new batch or a newly linked account applies at once. Package-private: it is a helper of the use cases, not a use case, so it checks no permission.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.application.LiveTimetableService
comment:
The live timetable: the lectures a person may see, in a date range. What a person sees follows their roles (Timetia ADR 0004):
  • the Super Admin sees every lecture ({@link AcademicPermissions#LIVE_VIEW_ALL});
  • a Super HOD, HOD, CR, BR or student sees the lectures of the places they hold the role in ({@link AcademicPermissions#LIVE_VIEW}): a department's, a division's, or those of a batch, which include the theory lectures of the batch's division;
  • a faculty member sees the lectures they teach ({@link AcademicPermissions#LIVE_VIEW_OWN}).

A list and a single lecture must agree: the list holds exactly the lectures the single-record decision would allow. The list is therefore filtered in the query from {@link Authorization#reach}, before it is paged, and a test holds the two together for every role. A lecture the caller may not see is answered as not found, so its existence is not revealed.

methods.name: divisionsOf
methods.comment: The divisions of these batches. A theory lecture is for every batch of its division, so holding a batch reaches them.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.application.LiveTimetableService$LiveFilter
comment: What a list is narrowed by; the date range is required, the rest are optional.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.application.NewEntry
comment: What is needed to add a lecture to a draft version.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.application.NewOccurrence
comment: A lecture on one date that publishing a version creates. It copies from the teaching assignment what cannot change: where the lecture is, what kind it is and who teaches it. It starts as the base timetable has it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.application.Occurrence
comment: A lecture on one date, as stored (ADR 0004): the slot the base timetable gave it, and the slot it has now once a change is laid over it. Who may see it is decided from {@link com.kibootia.backend.timetable.LectureView}, which adds what can change since it was created.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.application.OccurrenceQuery
comment: Which live lectures a list asks for: those in a date range that the caller may see, narrowed by optional filters. The store turns it into one query, so a page and its total are correct (the list is filtered before it is paged).

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.application.OccurrenceQuery$Visibility
comment: Where the caller may see lectures, as conditions on the occurrence's own columns. A lecture is visible when any one holds. Nothing here means the caller sees nothing, so the store must not be asked.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.application.OccurrenceStore
comment: Where the dated lectures are kept. The use cases depend on this port, never on JPA (ADR 0003). Only active lectures are ever returned; a lecture a later version replaced stays in the table, marked superseded, and is not seen. A cancelled lecture is active: it is shown, marked, until the term ends.

methods.name: insertAll
methods.comment: Stores the lectures, as the base timetable has them, and returns them in the same order.

methods.name: supersede
methods.comment: Marks the division's active lectures whose base date is from {@code from} up to but not including {@code toExclusive} superseded, because a version that takes effect in that range replaces them, and returns their IDs.

methods.name: countChanged
methods.comment: How many of those lectures have a change laid over them, which a new version must not discard.

methods.name: findAll
methods.comment: The active lectures among these IDs.

methods.name: lockAll
methods.comment: Like {@link #findAll}, but locks the lectures until the end of the transaction, in a fixed order, so changes queue.

methods.name: move
methods.comment: Moves the lecture to the slot and records the ticket.

methods.name: cancel
methods.comment: Cancels the lecture and records the ticket.

methods.name: search
methods.comment: A page of the active lectures the query allows, in date and time order unless the page asks otherwise.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.application.TimetableAuthoringService
comment:
The use cases that arrange the base timetable: a division's versions, the weekly entries of a draft, and publishing, which turns a draft into the dated lectures everyone sees. This is Super Admin configuration ({@link AcademicPermissions#CONFIG_MANAGE}), the manually arranged timetable of version 1 (Timetia ADR 0001).

A draft is edited freely; a published version is never changed. A version takes effect on its {@code effectiveFrom} date and until the next published version of the division does. Publishing checks the timetable cannot book a teacher, a room or a group of students twice, within the version and against what other divisions already have, and only then creates the dated lectures, in one transaction with replacing the ones the new version supersedes.

methods.name: publish
methods.comment: Makes a draft the timetable of its division from its effective date. The dated lectures are created from the effective date to the end of the term, or to the day before the next published version takes over, and the division's lectures in that range from earlier versions are superseded. All of it happens in one transaction: either the version is published with its lectures or nothing changes.

methods.name: rejectWhatOtherLecturesHold
methods.comment: A teacher or a room cannot be in two divisions' lectures at once, so what the new lectures need is checked against what other lectures hold. The lectures this version replaces have already let go. The database refuses a double booking anyway; this says what is in the way.

methods.name: validate
methods.comment: Checks a new entry and returns its teaching assignment; every bad field is reported together.

methods.name: requireEntry
methods.comment: An entry of this version; one that belongs to another version looks the same as one that does not exist.

methods.name: weekly
methods.comment: The entries as weekly lectures; one whose assignment can no longer be found is left out.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.application.TimetableAuthoringService$Published
comment: The result of publishing: the version, how many dated lectures it created and how many earlier ones it replaced.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.application.TimetableEntry
comment: One weekly lecture of a version: a teaching assignment placed on a day and time, in a room or online.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.application.TimetableProperties
comment: Timetable settings.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.application.TimetableStore
comment: Where timetable versions and their entries are kept. The use cases depend on this port, never on JPA (ADR 0003). Reads and writes act on the current tenant's rows.

methods.name: deleteVersion
methods.comment: Removes a version and its entries for good. Only a draft is ever removed.

methods.name: markPublished
methods.comment: Makes the version published.

methods.name: publishedStartingOn
methods.comment: Whether a published version of the division already takes effect on that date.

methods.name: nextPublishedAfter
methods.comment: The first date after {@code date} on which a published version of the division takes effect, if any.

methods.name: entriesOf
methods.comment: The entries of a version in a stable order: day, then start time.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.application.TimetableVersion
comment: A version of one division's base timetable (ADR 0004): the weekly pattern that applies from {@code effectiveFrom} (W.E.F.) until a later published version takes over, within one academic term.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.application.VersionStatus
comment: Where a timetable version is in its life. A draft is being arranged and has no effect; publishing it makes it the timetable from its effective date and fixes it: a published version is never edited.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.domain.ClaimKey
comment: One thing held for one hour of one date: the unit that must be unique. {@code hour} is the hour of day, 8 to 19.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.domain.ClaimKind
comment: What a lecture holds for an hour. Two lectures can never hold the same thing for the same hour, which is how a teacher, a room or a group of students is kept from being booked twice, whatever the order in which tickets are applied.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.domain.Claims
comment:
Works out what a lecture holds. A lecture holds, for each hour it lasts: its faculty member; its room, if it is held in person; and its students. A theory lecture is for the whole division, so it holds the division and every batch in it; a lab or tutorial is for one batch, so it holds only that. Two batches of a division can therefore have labs at the same time, while a theory lecture and a lab of one of its batches cannot overlap.

Hours are whole hours: a lecture from 09:00 to 11:00 holds the hours 9 and 10. Online lectures hold no room.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.domain.Clashes
comment:
Finds the double-bookings among the weekly entries of one draft version, so that a timetable being arranged is refused a lecture that would book a teacher, a room or students twice. Two lectures clash when their times overlap and they need the same faculty member, the same room, or the same students. Between divisions, and once lectures have dates, the same rule is kept by the claims every dated lecture holds ({@link Claims}), which the database enforces.

Students clash when the lectures are of the same division and either is for the whole division (a theory lecture, which has no batch) or both are for the same batch. Two different batches of one division may be taught at the same time, which is how labs run in parallel. Lectures of different divisions never share students here.

methods.name: within
methods.comment: Every pair of weekly lectures that clash, each pair once, with the first reason found for it.

methods.name: overlap
methods.comment: Whether two half-open time ranges share any time. Lectures that meet end to end do not overlap.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.domain.Clashes$Weekly
comment: A lecture that repeats weekly, as one entry of a version.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.domain.WeeklyDates
comment: Expands a weekly lecture into the dates it falls on.

methods.name: of
methods.comment: Every date from {@code from} to {@code to}, both included, that falls on the given day of the week (1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday), in order. Empty when the range is empty or contains no such day.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.persistence.JpaClaimStore
comment: Keeps what lectures hold in MySQL through JPA.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.persistence.JpaOccurrenceStore
comment: Keeps the dated lectures in MySQL through JPA.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.persistence.JpaTimetableStore
comment: Keeps timetable versions and their entries in MySQL through JPA.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.persistence.OccurrenceClaimEntity
comment: One thing a lecture holds for one hour. Persistence only (ADR 0004). The unique key on (tenant, kind, resource, date, hour) is in the migration: it is what keeps a teacher, a room or students from being booked twice.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.persistence.OccurrenceClaimRepository
comment: Claims in MySQL. Entity queries and the bulk delete are filtered by tenant on their own (ADR 0028).

methods.name: find
methods.comment: The claims on a kind of resource on some dates and hours. It can return a few more than the exact combinations asked for, because dates and hours are matched separately; the store narrows the answer.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.persistence.OccurrenceEntity
comment: The table row of a lecture on one date. Persistence only (ADR 0004). The base columns are the slot the base timetable gave the lecture and are never changed; the effective columns start equal to them and are what a change lays over the lecture. The row's version is the revision a change is checked against.

methods.name: moveTo
methods.comment: Lays a slot over the base.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.persistence.OccurrenceRepository
comment: Lectures in MySQL. Entity queries and the bulk update below are filtered by tenant on their own (ADR 0028), so none of them can reach another tenant's lectures.

methods.name: activeIdsBetween
methods.comment: The active lectures of a division whose base date is in the range: what a new version that starts there replaces.

methods.name: supersede
methods.comment: Marks lectures superseded. A bulk statement, so the update time is set here and the optimistic-lock version is left alone: nothing edits a lecture through the entity at the same time.

methods.name: lockActive
methods.comment: The active lectures among these IDs, locked until the end of the transaction, in ID order so that changes queue.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.persistence.OccurrenceSpecifications
comment: Turns an {@link OccurrenceQuery} into one query condition on the lecture's own columns. Where the caller may see lectures is part of the same condition as the date range and the filters, so the database filters before it pages and a page and its total are right. An empty set of places adds no condition for that kind rather than an {@code in ()}, and a visibility that allows nothing never reaches here (the service answers an empty page first).

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.persistence.OccurrenceStatus
comment: Whether a stored lecture still counts. A lecture a later version replaces is kept, marked superseded, rather than deleted, so the history of what was published stays; only active lectures are ever shown or checked.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.persistence.TimetableEntryEntity
comment: The table row of one weekly lecture of a version. Persistence only (ADR 0004).

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.persistence.TimetableEntryRepository
comment: Timetable entries in MySQL; entity queries are filtered by tenant on their own (ADR 0028).

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.persistence.TimetableMapper
comment: Converts between the timetable persistence entities and the application models by hand (ADR 0005).

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.persistence.TimetableVersionEntity
comment: The table row of a timetable version. Persistence only (ADR 0004). The generated {@code published_from} column and the unique key on it are in the migration; they keep two published versions of a division from taking effect on one day.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.persistence.TimetableVersionRepository
comment: Timetable versions in MySQL; entity queries are filtered by tenant on their own (ADR 0028).

methods.name: earliestEffectiveAfter
methods.comment: The earliest date after {@code date} on which a version with this status takes effect, or none.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.web.CreateEntryRequest
comment: The body of {@code POST /api/v1/timetable/versions/{id}/entries}: one weekly lecture of a draft. {@code dayOfWeek} is 1 (Monday) to 6 (Saturday); times are on the hour between 08:00 and 20:00. An in-person lecture needs {@code roomId}; an online one must not have it and may carry a {@code meetingLink}. The server checks all of it and reports each bad field.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.web.CreateVersionRequest
comment: The body of {@code POST /api/v1/timetable/versions}: a new draft for a division in a term. {@code effectiveFrom} is the W.E.F. date from which it applies; it must fall within the term.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.web.LiveLectureResponse
comment:
A lecture on one date as the live timetable shows it, with any applied change laid over the base timetable. The names and codes are those of the reference data as it is now, and are null if what they describe was deleted since the timetable was published. {@code batchId} is null for a theory lecture, which is for the whole division. {@code roomId} is null for an online lecture, which may have a meeting link.

A cancelled lecture is shown, marked {@code cancelled}, so nobody goes to it. A lecture that was moved is shown where it is now, marked {@code changed}, with the time the base timetable had it in the {@code original…} fields. The ticket that made the change is not shown: people see the result of a change, not the ticket.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.web.LiveTimetableController
comment: The live timetable: the lectures the signed-in person may see, by date. Everyone with a role in Timetia reads it, and what they see follows their role and place (see {@link LiveTimetableService}); a person with no role sees an empty list. It is read-only: changing a lecture is a ticket, not an edit of the timetable.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.web.PublishedVersionResponse
comment: The result of publishing a version: the version, and how many dated lectures it created and replaced.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.web.TimetableEntryResponse
comment: One weekly lecture of a version as the API returns it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.web.TimetableMapper
comment: Converts between API types and application types by hand (ADR 0005).

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.web.TimetableVersionResponse
comment: A timetable version as the API returns it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.web.TimetableVersionsController
comment: Arranging the base timetable: a division's versions, the weekly lectures of a draft, and publishing. Super Admin configuration; the service enforces the permission. Adding to or removing from a draft are sub-resources of the version, and publishing, which is not plain CRUD, is an action on it (ADR 0043).

methods.name: delete
methods.comment: Removes a draft and its lectures. A published version is never removed.

methods.name: entries
methods.comment: The lectures of a version by day and time. A version holds at most a week's worth, so it is not paged.

methods.name: publish
methods.comment: Makes the draft the division's timetable from its effective date: checks it books nothing twice, creates the dated lectures and replaces the ones it supersedes, all or nothing.
